card.title: MAORI BATTALION
card.text: Gets +2+2 when a friendly unit becomes Veteran.
card.flavorText: The 28th Māori Battalion was a light infantry battalion of the New Zealand Army which was part of the 2nd New Zealand Division during WWII. It was formed in 1940 after pressure from Māori leaders and organisations who wanted a distinct Māori unit for overseas service. The battalion, counting about 3,600 men in its ranks,r became one of New Zealand’s most decorated units of the war. It first served in Greece, where it fought at Petra Pass and helped cover the Allied withdrawal. In Crete, it took part in hard fighting after the German airborne landings, including a bayonet charge at the Battle of 42nd Street alongside the Australian 2/7th Battalion. In North Africa, it fought at Sollum, Gazala, Minqar Qaim, El Alamein, Tebaga Gap, and Takrouna. Second Lieutenant Moana-Nui-a-Kiwa Ngarimu received the Victoria Cross for his actions at Point 209. In Italy, the battalion fought at Orsogna, Cassino, Florence, Faenza, and during the final river crossings toward Trieste. It was disbanded in 1946 after returning to New Zealand.
